Sie beraten Forschende sowie zentrale Stellen der ETH Zürich und begleiten Projekte an der Schnittstelle von Wissenschaft, Technologieentwicklung und Anwendung.

Dabei arbeiten Sie regelmässig an Vorhaben mit technischem und wirtschaftlichem Bezug, insbesondere im Zusammenhang mit Forschungskooperationen, Industriepartnerschaften, Material- und Technologietransfer sowie projektbezogenen Know-how-Fragestellungen.

Ihre Tätigkeit umfasst die **selbständige Ausarbeitung, Prüfung und Verhandlung von Verträgen** mit nationalen und internationalen Partnern sowie die rechtliche Begleitung komplexer projektbezogener Fragestellungen.
## Stellenbeschreibung ##
**Erarbeitung, Prüfung und Verhandlung von Verträgen** für Forschungsprojekte, insbesondere in den Bereichen Materialwissenschaften, Chemie und Maschinenbau, mit nationalen und internationalen Partnern (z.B. Forschungskooperationen, Industriekooperationen, Materialtransfer, Technologietransfer und Vertraulichkeitsvereinbarungen).
**Beratung und Unterstützung der Forschenden** bei rechtlichen und vertraglichen Fragestellungen im Zusammenhang mit technologieorientierten Forschungsprojekten, insbesondere bei Kooperationen mit Industriepartnern und anderen akademischen Einrichtungen.
**Enge Zusammenarbeit mit zentralen Schnittstellen**, insbesondere dem Rechtsdienst, ETH transfer und weiteren internen Fachstellen, zur Sicherstellung kohärenter rechtlicher Lösungen.
**Koordination mit internen und externen Stakeholdern**, einschliesslich Forschenden, Industriepartnern, Hochschulen, Forschungsinstitutionen und weiteren Projektpartnern.
**Mitwirkung bei der Weiterentwicklung und Standardisierung von Prozessen** für technologieorientierte Forschungsprojekte innerhalb der ETH Zürich, mit Fokus auf effiziente, rechtssichere und praxistaugliche Abläufe.
**Konzeption und Durchführung von Informationsveranstaltungen und Schulungen** für Forschende zu rechtlichen Aspekten von Forschungsverträgen, Industriekooperationen und technologieorientierten Projekten.
**Aktive Mitgestaltung des Vertragsportfolios**, insbesondere in den Bereichen Materialwissenschaften, Chemie und Maschinenbau, innerhalb der Forschungsvertragsgruppe.
## Profil ##
Wir suchen eine integrative Persönlichkeit, die komplexe Sachverhalte schnell durchdringt und Freude an der engen Zusammenarbeit in einem diversen Umfeld hat.
* **Ausbildung:** Sie verfügen über einen Schweizer Hochschulabschluss in Rechtswissenschaften.
**Erfahrung:** Von Vorteil ist Erfahrung in einem industriellen Umfeld oder an der Schnittstelle zwischen Industrie und Hochschule. Idealerweise bringen Sie ein Verständnis dafür mit, wie unterschiedliche Interessen in Forschungskooperationen rechtlich und praktisch zusammengeführt werden können.
* **Kompetenzen:** Sie besitzen ausgezeichnete **analytische und konzeptionelle Fähigkeiten**, **Verhandlungsgeschick** und **Durchsetzungsvermögen** sowie die Fähigkeit, sich schnell in neue Themen einzuarbeiten und flexibel mit **komplexen Sachverhalten** umzugehen. Eine schnelle Auffassungsgabe und ein hohes Mass an **Eigenverantwortung** zeichnen Sie ebenso aus wie eine **effiziente und exakte Arbeitsweise**.
* **Sprachen:** Sie kommunizieren und verhandeln stilsicher in **Deutsch **und **Englisch **(Wort und Schrift). Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil.
* **Mindset:** Sie arbeiten **effizient, exakt** und **lösungsorientiert** und verfügen über einen ausgeprägten **Team**geist und hohe **Sozialkompetenz**. Sie verfügen über das im Drittmittelwesen einer Hochschule notwendige Gespür, wo Wissenschaftler **rasch** und **pragmatisch** unterstützt werden müssen.
Durch das Formulieren von klaren und eindeutigen vertraglichen Regelungen legen Sie die Basis für die spätere praktische Umsetzung der Forschungsergebnisse. Sie sind in der Lage, ein **heterogenes Portfolio an Geschäften eigenständig zu organisieren** und termingerecht zu erledigen. Indem Sie zügig, lösungsorientiert und umsichtig arbeiten, ermöglichen Sie den Forschenden die Durchführung ihrer exzellenten Projekte.
Wenn Sie darüber hinaus Interesse an naturwissenschaftlichen, technischen und wirtschaftlichen Zusammenhängen haben, bringen Sie ideale Voraussetzungen mit.
Werden Sie Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur Ihre berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt. Wir engagieren uns für eine nachhaltige und klimaneutrale Hochschule.
## Wir bieten ##
* Ein grosses, erfahrenes Team von Juristen;
* Zahlreiche Vergünstigungen, wie z.B. ÖV-Abonnemente und Car Sharing, ein breites Sportangebot des ASVZ, Kinderbetreuung sowie attraktive Vorsorgeleistungen;
* Flexibles Arbeiten und Möglichkeit für Homeoffice.
Arbeiten, Lehren und Forschen an der ETH Zürich
## Diversität und Nachhaltigkeit sind uns wichtig ##
Im Einklang mit unseren Werten unterstützt die ETH Zürich eine inklusive Kultur. Wir fördern Chancengleichheit, schätzen Vielfalt und pflegen ein Arbeits- und Lernumfeld, in dem die Rechte und die Würde aller Mitarbeitenden und Studierenden respektiert werden.

Auf unserer Webseite zur Chancengleichheit und Vielfalt erfahren Sie, wie wir ein faires und offenes Umfeld sicherstellen, in dem sich alle entwickeln und entfalten können. Nachhaltigkeit ist für uns ein zentraler Wert - wir arbeiten konsequent an einer klimaneutralen Zukunft.

Bitte bewerben Sie sich ausschliesslich über das Online-Bewerbungsportal. Bewerbungen per E-Mail sowie auf dem Postweg werden nicht berücksichtigt.

This is a builder role.

You will translate the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, GDPR, the CCPA/CPRA, and emerging global AI and privacy requirements into pragmatic policies, standards, and assessment workflows - and partner with Enterprise Risk, Security, Product, Compliance, Legal, Regulatory, Engineering, and Data Science to make them real.

Help build, roll out, and embed Adyen's enterprise-wide AI governance framework, policies, and standards, driving consistency as AI adoption scales across the business.

Design simple, proportionate, risk-tiered processes and “green paths” that make responsible AI the easy path for fast-moving teams - using clear risk tiers and practical incentives so the compliant route is also the most convenient one.
Translate model-evaluation techniques - including fairness, bias, and adversarial (red-teaming) testing - into clear procedures that technology teams can apply to their own models and tools.
Partner with Enterprise Risk, Security, Product, Compliance, Legal, Regulatory, and Engineering to run the AI governance program and align on controls, escalation, and human-oversight protocols.
Advise on privacy considerations across the AI lifecycle, coordinating with the wider DPO Office on the interaction between AI assessments and data protection.
Design and deliver AI governance training and promote AI literacy and a culture of responsible, accountable AI use.
Monitor global AI and privacy developments and translate them into proportionate governance requirements, supporting responses to audit, regulatory, and client inquiries.

We’re looking for a Senior Legal Counsel to join our team at Monzo to support our payments business including digital assets and emerging payment technologies. You will report to Monzo’s Director of Legal for Payments & Business Banking, be part of the Legal and Board Governance Collective, and act as a legal business partner for the teams working on these initiatives.
This role sits at the intersection of payments, digital assets and emerging payments technologies. You’ll help teams navigate a rapidly evolving legal and regulatory landscape, helping Monzo innovate responsibly while protecting our customers.
You’ll work at all levels in the organisation and with a wide-range of stakeholders from Product Managers and Designers, to Operations professionals and Software Engineers, and Risk, FinCrime and Compliance professionals.
While payments, digital assets and emerging financial technologies will be your primary focus, more broadly, you will also have opportunities to work within a team of product lawyers to give first rate legal advice and support to Monzo’s Product Collectives, including in areas like personal and business banking.
🔑You’ll play a key role by...
You’ll work directly with senior lawyers, product managers and engineers to provide legal advice and commercial insights to develop and grow Monzo Bank in the UK - and internationally.

Partner with product managers to advise on legal matters, in particular relating to the impact of digital assets and emerging financial technologies, and advise on the legal and regulatory requirements for Monzo.
Help to develop efficient ways of working to enable Monzo to scale quickly, and ensuring Monzo operates safely and in accordance with the law and regulation.
Provide training and knowledge sharing with other Monzonauts on the impact of laws and regulations for Monzo and our customers in your specialist area..
Often act as the sole lawyer advising product managers or other colleagues, identifying legal issues proactively, evaluating relevant risks and finding effective solutions to unique and complex business activities.
You’ll work closely and collaboratively with Monzo’s Director of Legal for Payments & Business Banking, Director of Product Legal, the General Counsel of Monzo Bank Limited and the other members of the UK Legal team to provide legal advice and commercial insights, in particular in relation to digital assets and other emerging financial technologies, to Product teams.
You’ll be a trusted advisor and will work proactively and collaboratively with other relevant stakeholders and teams across the Monzo Group, including the Product, Risk & Compliance, Supplier Operations, Financial Crime, Fraud and Operations teams.
You’ll advise on the evolving legal and regulatory framework for digital assets and emerging financial technologies, working with colleagues across the UK and EU to to help us identify relevant local legal and regulatory requirements and apply them to our products.
You’ll work with colleagues across the Legal and Board Governance Collective to improve the management of our teams’ activities, including through identifying suitable technology solutions to streamline workflows, optimise processes and efficiencies, and increase scalability.
You’ll proactively manage relationships with external suppliers and law firms to enhance processes around cost management to ensure we are optimising our spend and extracting best value while delivering top-quality legal support.
🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…
You are a technically excellent lawyer with a minimum of 5 years of relevant post-qualification experience, with recent experience of digital assets, emerging financial technologies and the evolving regulatory regime.
You have demonstrated experience of advising on laws and regulations relevant to financial services, including the UK regulatory regime as it applies to digital assets and emerging payment technologies.
You are a team player and a keen problem solver, skilled at assessing risk and recommending solutions that balance commercial and risk considerations. You think ahead, anticipate relevant challenges, understand the commercial objectives of the teams you support, set clear objectives, and find effective solutions.
You are proactive, take initiative to broaden your knowledge, and are passionate about the intersection of banking and technology and the transformation unfolding in consumer finance. You are excited to work in a fast-paced environment and to join us for the next stage of our journey at Monzo!

EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs) To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the five Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) and the Intelligence Community Senior Officer Core Qualification (ICSOCQ) listed below in your resume. RESUMES MUST NOT EXCEED TWO (2) PAGES.

Resumes over the two (2)-page limit will not be reviewed and will be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, educations, and accomplishments applicable to the qualifications. If your resume does not demonstrate evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position.

For more information regarding ECQs, please visit the Executive Core Qualifications page on the OPM website.

ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and Principles of the American Founding This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people.

ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades.

ECQ 3: Merit and Competence This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality.

ECQ 4: Leading People This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable.

ECQ 5: Achieving Results This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors.

ISCOCQ: Leading the Intelligence Enterprise This core qualification involves the ability to integrate resources, information, interests, and activities effectively in support of the Intelligence Community's mission and to lead and leverage cross-organizational collaborative networks to achieve significant mission results.

Inherent to this senior officer qualification is a deep understanding of the intelligence enterprise and a shared commitment to the IC's core values.

Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM-approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs.

Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualification Review Board (QRB)) or your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

In-depth knowledge of the mission and legal issues affecting the IC. Superior ability to think creatively to solve complex and novel legal issues.

They are an effective communicator who can provide clear, authoritative written and oral guidance to senior leadership and stakeholders across the organization. About the Office: The Justice Management Division (JMD) is the administrative arm of the Department of Justice (DOJ), headed by the Assistant Attorney General for Administration (AAG/A), who is also the Chief Financial Officer for the Department.

The JMD Office of the General Counsel (OGC) functions as "in-house" counsel to the AAG/A, JMD managers, and senior Department leadership on a wide variety of matters relating to the organization, management, and administration of the Department.

OGC attorneys advise JMD and Department management in areas such as appropriations, budget and financial management, agency organizational management, personnel, procurement, access to government records (FOIA and Privacy Act), security, and delegations of authority.

OGC attorneys also litigate in administrative forums and assist litigating divisions and U.S. Attorney's Offices (USAOs) when JMD matters are in the federal courts. Job Description: This position uses the organizational title of Assistant General Counsel and reports to a JMD Deputy General Counsel.

The incumbent also has significant collaborative interaction with the General Counsel, attorney colleagues in the office, and managers and attorneys throughout JMD and the Department.

As an Assistant General Counsel, you will: Provide legal advice to JMD management, JMD staffs, and other DOJ components on matters of appropriations law, in order to assist in the development of DOJ's budget and the enactment of DOJ's Appropriations Act, and to assure DOJ's compliance with appropriations law in the pursuit of its mission.

Specific topics may include: the permissible use and availability of appropriated funds, proposed language for the President's Budget and appropriations bills, reprogrammings and transfers, agency reorganizations, reimbursable agreements, lapses in appropriations, compliance with the Antideficiency Act, and government travel, among others.

Review Department policies related to appropriations and financial management. Provide appropriations law training to Department personnel.

The work of the attorney selected for this position involves research, review, and analysis of relevant statutes, regulations, Office of Legal Counsel and Government Accountability Office opinions, Office of Management and Budget guidance, administrative and judicial decisions, and other applicable authorities to provide legal advice to Department of Justice managers and offices to assist them to formulate agency policy or to make difficult management decisions.

The attorney selected for this position may also have the opportunity to work in OGC's other practice areas.
Qualifications: OGC is looking for candidates with experience in federal appropriations law. Experience in OGC's other practice areas may be helpful but is not required.

The Office is interested in candidates with demonstrated ability to efficiently and thoroughly research and incisively analyze a wide variety of complex issues; to express themselves clearly and persuasively in oral and written presentations; to exercise sound judgment; to manage a workload consisting of a number of varied projects, without specific guidelines and often with short deadlines; and to contribute to and work in a supportive and collaborative environment.

Applicants must be United States citizens, have a J.D. degree from an accredited law school, be an active member in good standing of the bar of any state (or the District of Columbia), and have no less than four years post-J.D. legal experience.

This is Adyen
Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.

The Global DPO Office is expanding its presence across regions, with team members currently based in Amsterdam and New York and plans to grow in APAC. We own Adyen’s global privacy program and AI governance, and support incident response and data governance across the business.

This means working across teams and regions to turn privacy and data protection requirements into practical ways of working, while helping Adyen respond effectively when issues arise and navigate new challenges around AI and data.
The work is varied, high-impact, and often complex. We work closely with colleagues across Adyen to solve problems that don’t always have straightforward answers, balancing regulatory requirements with the needs of a fast-growing, global business. We give people the space to take ownership, develop their expertise, and shape how we approach new and evolving challenges together.

We are looking for a driven and enthusiastic Senior Privacy Counsel to join our Global DPO Office in Singapore and drive our privacy work across the APAC region. Working closely with your colleagues in Amsterdam and New York, you will extend and strengthen our global privacy framework across the diverse and fast-evolving regulatory landscape of the Asia-Pacific region, enabling Adyen to grow in some of our most important commercial markets while making responsible choices.
This is a builder role. Winning in APAC is one of Adyen's top commercial priorities, and you will be central to it - establishing a scalable regional privacy baseline, advising on complex local data processing and localization requirements, and partnering closely with regional product, engineering, commercial, and second-line teams.

You must combine strong analytical and communication skills with pragmatic, strategic thinking as you advise internal and external stakeholders, including, at times, local regulators.

Act as the senior privacy advisor for Adyen's APAC operations, providing pragmatic, business-aligned guidance to regional product, engineering, commercial, HR, and corporate teams.
Adapt and extend Adyen's global privacy framework, standards, and policies to meet regional requirements, establishing a consistent and scalable privacy baseline across APAC jurisdictions.
Advise on and help operationalize privacy compliance across the APAC region, spanning major regimes such as Singapore's PDPA, India's DPDPA, Japan's APPI, Australia's Privacy Act, and Hong Kong's PDPO, as well as navigating cross-border data flows, localization requirements, and the extraterritorial reach of regional privacy laws..
Advise on cross-border data transfers, data localization, and localized consent flows across the region, in close coordination with regional product and engineering hubs.
Conduct and review privacy impact assessments, data protection impact assessments, and records of processing activities for APAC-specific initiatives and entities.
Anticipate and identify data protection obligations and risks, and help address them in a practical, scalable, and privacy-by-design manner.
Draft, review, and negotiate privacy terms in commercial agreements, vendor arrangements, and data processing agreements relevant to the region.
Monitor legislative and regulatory developments across APAC, interpret their impact for Adyen, and translate them into actionable internal policies, procedures, and controls.
Support privacy incident response and management in the region, coordinating with the wider DPO Office and relevant stakeholders.
Provide extended regional coverage on AI governance and broader data-related legal advisory, including data governance and retention, across APAC.
Develop and deliver region-specific privacy training and self-service resources, fostering a strong culture of privacy accountability and awareness across APAC.
Engage with regional stakeholders and, where appropriate, local regulators and external counsel, building trusted relationships that strengthen Adyen's regional privacy capability.

You are a qualified lawyer in a Common-wealth jurisdiction.
You have 7+ years of relevant data privacy experience, including GDPR and a strong command of APAC privacy regimes.
You have deep, hands-on expertise in two or more APAC privacy frameworks (e.g., PDPA, DPDPA, APPI, PIPA, PDPO, PIPL) and a strong grasp of the wider regional landscape, including cross-border data-transfer and localization requirements.
You have experience setting up or scaling a privacy program in-house, and you know how to build a baseline that works across many different countries; law firm experience is also valued.
You are a generalist comfortable across commercial negotiations, compliance frameworks, vendor assessments, incident management, data transfers, data protection impact assessments, and privacy by design.
You are experienced at cross-functional partnering across engineering, product, legal, compliance, and enterprise risk, and confident engaging with regional stakeholders and, at times, local regulators.
Experience in payments, financial services, or fintech is strongly preferred, though not essential.
Knowledge of emerging AI regulation and AI governance frameworks (such as the EU AI Act and IMDA's Model AI Governance Framework) is a plus.
Relevant certifications such as CIPP/E, CIPP/A, CIPM, or AIGP are an advantage.
You have the ability to structure and prioritize in a high-volume, fast-paced environment, and to build and drive processes to completion.
You have strong drafting, communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with a proactive, builder mindset and a strong sense of ownership.
You are fluent in English, both written and spoken.

# Conseiller juridique / Spécialiste des contrats pour l'ETH Zurich | Espace #
L'ETH Zurich est l'une des universités les plus prestigieuses au monde dans les domaines des sciences et de l'ingénierie. Grâce à son initiative stratégique, **ETH Zurich - Space** étend systématiquement ses activités dans la recherche et la technologie spatiales.

Un environnement unique d'innovation est créé par le recrutement de chercheurs de haut calibre de renommée internationale et l'expansion des collaborations avec des partenaires de premier plan issus du monde académique, des agences spatiales et de l'industrie.
Au sein de la Vice-présidence pour le transfert de connaissances et les relations d'entreprise, le groupe des contrats de recherche soutient les chercheurs afin de garantir que leurs projets avec des partenaires nationaux et internationaux reposent sur une base juridique solide.
Pour renforcer notre équipe, nous recherchons, avec effet immédiat ou selon accord, une personne engagée, orientée solutions et forte négociatrice pour assumer le rôle de Conseiller juridique pour ETH Zurich - Space.
## Description du poste ##
**Votre rôle à l'interface entre la recherche spatiale et le droit**
Dans ce rôle, vous serez le principal point de contact juridique pour les activités de recherche d'ETH Zurich - Space et ETH Swiss GeoLab. Vous ferez partie d'une équipe solide d'environ 20 professionnels du droit au sein du groupe des contrats de recherche, où vous bénéficierez de leur large expertise et d'un échange mutuel d'idées.

Votre attention personnelle sera portée sur la gestion autonome du portefeuille lié à l'espace.

Dans un contexte d'un nombre croissant de collaborations, vous faciliterez et encouragerez la conclusion de contrats entre les chercheurs de l'ETH et les organisations liées à l'espace - allant des entreprises industrielles et start-ups aux agences spatiales internationales, ainsi qu'aux institutions académiques et publiques.

Vous conseillerez les chercheurs et la direction sur la rédaction et la négociation de contrats de recherche complexes et aiderez à garantir que les projets de recherche innovants soient mis en œuvre de manière juridiquement solide et efficace.

Cela englobe à la fois les technologies spatiales traditionnelles (par exemple le matériel) et l'observation de la Terre, le traitement de l'information géographique et l'utilisation des données spatiales sur Terre.

Ce faisant, vous jouez également un rôle de pont avec les parties prenantes suisses dans les organismes gouvernementaux et le secteur économique.
Vous soutiendrez les scientifiques dans leurs projets depuis l'idée initiale de collaboration jusqu'à la conclusion d'un contrat et poserez les bases juridiques pour une recherche internationale de classe mondiale dans un environnement très dynamique.
**Vos principales responsabilités**
* Vous examinerez, rédigerez et négocierez de manière autonome des contrats de recherche et développement complexes nationaux et internationaux, en particulier des accords de collaboration de recherche, des accords de consortium, des accords de confidentialité (NDA) et d'autres accords de recherche et de coopération.
* Vous gérerez des projets avec des agences spatiales internationales, des institutions de recherche et des partenaires industriels, notamment dans le cadre de l'Agence spatiale européenne (ESA), de la NASA, du Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) et d'autres partenaires spatiaux et de recherche internationaux.
* Vous conseillerez les chercheurs et les gestionnaires de projets sur les questions juridiques relatives aux collaborations internationales de recherche, à la propriété intellectuelle, aux questions de responsabilité et autres risques contractuels.
* Vous apporterez un soutien sur les questions relatives aux contrôles à l'exportation et aux biens à double usage, en travaillant en étroite collaboration avec les unités de conformité concernées à l'ETH Zurich.
* Vous fournirez des conseils proactifs et orientés solutions aux chercheurs et gestionnaires de projets tout au long du cycle de vie du projet - de l'initiation à la réussite du projet.
* Vous développerez davantage les modèles de contrats, les lignes directrices et les processus standards pour une gestion efficace et conforme aux exigences légales des projets spatiaux et de recherche.
* Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec le transfert ETH, les unités de conformité et d'autres parties prenantes internes et externes.
* Vous contribuerez de manière significative à garantir que les collaborations internationales de recherche soient juridiquement solides, tout en préservant la capacité d'action de la communauté de recherche.
## Profil ##
Nous recherchons une personne capable de saisir rapidement des questions complexes, de développer des solutions pragmatiques et qui prend plaisir à soutenir les chercheurs dans un environnement de recherche international de premier plan.
* **Formation :** Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme universitaire en droit (ou qualification juridique équivalente) combiné à une solide compréhension des contextes techniques.
* **Expérience :** Vous avez au moins 5 ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente en droit international des contrats ou en gestion de la recherche - idéalement acquise dans une organisation internationale, une entreprise du secteur technologique/spatial, une autorité liée à l'espace ou une université. Une expérience avec des contrats d'agences spatiales (par ex. ESA) ou d'entreprises spatiales est un atout majeur.
* **Expertise :** Vous possédez une connaissance approfondie du droit suisse et international des contrats. Une expérience en droit de la propriété intellectuelle, transfert de technologie ou droit de la recherche est un avantage.
* **Droit spatial** : Une connaissance du droit spatial international, des questions réglementaires liées au secteur spatial et du contexte de la politique scientifique des collaborations internationales de recherche serait un plus.
* **Contrôle à l'exportation & réglementation :** Une expérience en droit du contrôle à l'exportation (notamment ITAR/EAR), dans la gestion des biens à double usage ou dans des environnements réglementaires comparables est particulièrement bienvenue. La connaissance des cadres réglementaires liés à l'ESA ou à la NASA est un avantage supplémentaire.
* **Compétences :** Vous possédez d'excellentes compétences analytiques et conceptuelles, de solides compétences en négociation et la capacité d'aborder les risques juridiques de manière pragmatique et orientée solutions.
* **Langues :** Vous communiquez et négociez couramment en allemand et en anglais (à l'oral comme à l'écrit). Un anglais professionnel est essentiel.
* **État d'esprit & style de travail :** Vous vous caractérisez par une forte orientation service et une approche pragmatique et orientée solutions dans votre travail. Vous êtes un communicateur talentueux et êtes à l'aise dans vos interactions avec les chercheurs, les représentants de l'industrie et les autorités réglementaires.
